refs.quote: NORVASC ® is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure. Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular events, primarily strokes and myocardial infarctions.

The usual initial antihypertensive oral dose of NORVASC is 5 mg once daily, and the maximum dose is 10 mg once daily. Small, fragile, or elderly patients, or patients with hepatic insufficiency may be started on 2.5 mg once daily

regimens.dose_text: Usual initial oral dose: 5 mg once daily (2.5 mg once daily in small, fragile, elderly, or hepatic insufficiency patients, or when adding to other antihypertensive therapy). Maximum dose: 10 mg once daily. Wait 7 to 14 days between titration steps.

refs.quote: The effective antihypertensive oral dose in pediatric patients ages 6–17 years is 2.5 mg to 5 mg once daily. Doses in excess of 5 mg daily have not been studied in pediatric patients

regimens.dose_text: 2.5 mg to 5 mg orally once daily in pediatric patients ages 6 to 17 years. Doses in excess of 5 mg daily have not been studied in pediatric patients.

mechanism_of_action.value: Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium antagonist that selectively inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, with a greater effect on vascular smooth muscle cells. It acts as a peripheral arterial vasodilator to reduce peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure.

The limited available data based on post-marketing reports with NORVASC use in pregnant women are not sufficient to inform a drug-associated risk for major birth defects and miscarriage. There are risks to the mother and fetus associated with poorly controlled hypertension in pregnancy

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: No boxed warning or pregnancy contraindication; limited post-marketing human data are insufficient to inform risk; animal studies showed no teratogenicity at 10-20x MRHD, though rats had decreased litter size (~50%), 5-fold increase in intrauterine deaths, and prolonged gestation/labor at 10x MRHD; untreated hypertension carries maternal/fetal risks.
